ohPrimer.summary: ohPrimer (branded "Trellis" in-app) is an 8065-line single-file PWA: a family reading engine welding fast intake (RSVP/parafoveal/scroll/speak modes) to SM-2 spaced repetition. Four screens (Home/profiles, Library, Reader, Review) plus ~10 modals. Intake: EPUB (JSZip, TOC nav+NCX, figure blobs, front-matter skip), PDF (pdf.js with column/footnote heuristics, Tesseract OCR fallback), TXT/MD (table/code/divider heuristics), paste, URL article extraction, Gutenberg (Gutendex), RSS/Atom+podcast feeds (iTunes search, auto-discovery, OPML, conditional GET, auto-download), .ohcourse curriculum import, AI-generated passages, and audio transcription. On-device ML via pinned @xenova/transformers@2.17.2 from esm.sh (?bundle): Whisper-tiny.en (~40MB, ENGLISH-ONLY; sourceLang hardcoded eng_Latn), NLLB-200-distilled-600M (~612MB, 22 langs), SpeechT5+CMU-ARCTIC x-vectors (~200MB, 4 preset "clone" voices), Kokoro-82M (~86MB, ~54 voices). MODEL_SIZES_MB at index.html:6834. All inference forced single-thread WASM (GH Pages lacks COOP/COEP; no WebGPU on v2). A blob-URL module worker (index.html:6913-7089) runs all four tasks with per-task sticky fallback to main thread; worker evictExcept (6924) keeps exactly ONE model resident. Downloads: sticky consent gate with metered-connection warning, cumulative progress + 90s stall watchdog, "cancel" merely abandons the promise (transformers v2 has no AbortSignal) relying on browser-cache range resume. Transcripts persist ONLY after full completion (7807) — no checkpointing; the worker call inherits runInWorker's 120s default timeout, so any real podcast times out, sets sticky worker-off, re-decodes and reruns on the main thread. Whole episodes are buffered in memory (300MB cap) and decoded/resampled to one giant Float32Array. Storage: localStorage "openhearth_primer_v01" (profiles/prefs/feeds/consents); IndexedDB "openhearth_primer_db" v3 with stores books(byProfile,byLastRead), extracts(byProfile,byBook,byNextReview), episodes(byFeed,byGuid,byPublished,byProfile — also holds voice-clone WAVs under clone:* ids); model weights in browser cache; sw.js network-first shell + SWR CDN cache. Cloud sync removed (functions dormant, entry points throw). rebuild/ has 108 passing node tests over 7 ported modules (utils, state, privacy, tokenizer, partial parsers, partial learning/SM-2, comms); reader rendering, UI/modals, feeds UI, the entire ML layer (60-ai), and init/SW have NO module tests — only 11 Playwright behavior tests and 2 visual scripts. Docs: VISION, 7 ADRs, Diátaxis set, v0.1 robustness spec.

jank.symptom: Successful transcripts take ages; UI can freeze during them
jank.root_cause: Worker transcribe inherits runInWorker's 120s default timeout (index.html:7073-7078; call at 7762 passes no timeoutMs). Any real podcast exceeds 2 min on single-thread WASM whisper-tiny (numThreads=1 forced because GH Pages sends no COOP/COEP — 6822-6827; pinned transformers 2.17.2 predates WebGPU), so the worker is killed mid-inference, _workerTranscribeOk goes sticky-false, and the ENTIRE audio is re-decoded and re-transcribed on the main thread (7771-7775) — double work plus a frozen tab. No inference progress is shown either way (only model-file download %).
jank.fix_direction: Pass a duration-scaled or infinite timeout for transcribe (keep the watchdog for load only), stream per-chunk progress/results from the worker, and keep inference off-main permanently; longer-term serve with COOP/COEP or upgrade to transformers v3 for threads/WebGPU.

jank.symptom: Failed transcripts, especially long episodes on mobile
jank.root_cause: Everything is buffered in RAM end-to-end: fetchBinaryWithProxies accumulates up to 300MB of chunks (7848-7871), then loadAudioTo16k decodeAudioData's the whole file AND renders a full-length 16kHz Float32Array via OfflineAudioContext (7703-7713) — a 3h episode is ~700MB of samples, and the worker path immediately makes another copy (audio.slice() at 7761). iOS Safari's ~1GB tab budget OOMs. The transcript is persisted ONLY after full completion (persistNewBook at 7807) — no checkpointing — so a backgrounded/killed mobile tab loses everything, and enclosure fetches ride flaky public CORS proxies (cors.eu.org/allorigins, 7843).
jank.fix_direction: Chunked decode+transcribe (fixed-size windows fed to Whisper's stride API), checkpoint partial transcript + resume offset in the episodes store per chunk, stream fetch to IDB blob instead of RAM, drop the extra copies.

jank.root_cause: Up to 612MB (NLLB) fetched by transformers v2 which exposes no AbortSignal — Cancel (7115-7118) just abandons the promise while bytes keep flowing; resume relies on opaque browser-cache range behavior with no first-class resume UI (README:76, docs/limitations.md). Stall watchdog only fires after 90s of zero progress (7128). Weights live in the evictable browser cache, not the SW cache (sw.js:9-10), so an eviction silently re-triggers the whole download. Kokoro path shows per-file % without MB totals (7562). Everything imports from esm.sh at runtime — a CDN outage bricks all ML.
jank.fix_direction: Own the download: fetch model files with AbortController + Content-Range resume into Cache Storage/OPFS, show real MB progress and a persistent resume card, then point transformers at the local cache (or upgrade to v3 which supports custom cache).

jank.symptom: Whisper produces garbage for non-English podcasts
jank.root_cause: Model is Xenova/whisper-tiny.en — English-only (6950, 7735) — and addAudioFile hardcodes sourceLang "eng_Latn" (7801-7802), so translation of transcripts also assumes English source. No model-size/language choice.
jank.fix_direction: Offer multilingual whisper-tiny/base variants with a language picker; store detected language on the book record.

jank.symptom: Switching between Speak/Translate/Transcribe features is slow every time
jank.root_cause: Worker evictExcept (6924-6930) disposes every model except the one in use, and the main thread mirrors this (7113-7114, 7330-7333) for iOS's ~1GB budget — so each feature switch pays full ONNX session re-init (weights come from cache but session build is seconds-to-minutes single-threaded). Sticky _worker*Ok flags (7155,7444,7579,7743) also mean one transient worker failure demotes that feature to main-thread for the whole session.
jank.fix_direction: Keep memory budget but make eviction platform-aware (desktop can hold 2+ models), persist session-init state where possible, and let sticky flags reset after a cooldown or on explicit retry.

jank.symptom: Translation strip stalls on first use and per-block thereafter
jank.root_cause: First block triggers the full ~612MB NLLB download inline (renderTranslationStrip → translateViaWorkerOrMain → loadNllb, 7195-7258); every new block is a separate on-demand forward pass with no prefetch of upcoming blocks; cache is per-book per-language stored inside the ever-rewritten book record.
jank.fix_direction: Prefetch next N blocks in the worker while reading; consider a smaller default model tier.

jank.symptom: Voice-clone synthesis takes 5-15 minutes and blocks the feature
jank.root_cause: readCurrentDocInVoice synthesizes the ENTIRE document up front through SpeechT5 sentence-chunks before any audio plays (7483-7518); settings hint itself admits 5-15 min for a 30-min episode (index.html:1077). Cache is all-or-nothing per (book,preset).
jank.fix_direction: Stream playback as chunks complete (queue WAV pieces into MediaSource/sequential Audio) and checkpoint partial synthesis.

jank.symptom: Feed/article/episode fetches intermittently fail or rate-limit
jank.root_cause: Dependence on three public CORS proxies (cors.eu.org, allorigins, codetabs — 3524, 7843) for any host without CORS headers; proxies strip conditional-GET headers (3615) and rate-limit; acknowledged in README:75.
jank.fix_direction: Optional self-hosted proxy setting, or native-app path; batch feed refreshes through a single proxy session.

jank.symptom: Position autosave rewrites megabytes; storage churn
jank.root_cause: Book records store the full parsed blocks + figureBlobs + translations in one IDB record; saveCurrentPosition re-reads and rewrites the whole record whenever position changes (3319-3328, comment admits a positions-store migration was deliberately skipped).
jank.fix_direction: In the rebuild, split position/lastReadAt (and translations) into a small sibling store keyed by bookId.

jank.symptom: Rebuild is half-done; the riskiest code has no unit tests
jank.root_cause: rebuild/ has 108 tests but only for utils/state/privacy/tokenizer/partial-parsers/SM-2/comms (manifest.json scripts vs scriptsTodo). Reader modes (30-reader), UI/modals (35-ui), feeds UI (45-content), the ENTIRE ML layer (60-ai), and init/SW (90-init) exist only in index.html with zero module tests — exactly the layer the owner's complaints live in. EPUB/PDF parsers also unported (deferred H1/H8).
jank.fix_direction: Port 60-ai next with the worker protocol behind a testable seam (mock pipeline), since that's where downloads/transcription bugs concentrate; keep porting method from rebuild/README (verbatim extraction, issue-ID regression tests).

jank.symptom: Episodes store fields never populated; per-profile leakage
jank.root_cause: episodes store declares byGuid/byProfile indexes (1287-1290) but records written by audDl/autoDownloadQueue/putCachedClone never set guid or profileIdx — cached audio and voice clones are global across profiles, and profile deletion (5260-1283) cleans books+extracts but leaves episode blobs orphaned.
jank.fix_direction: Stamp profileIdx/guid on write; include episodes in profile-delete cascade and in the (orphaned) storage-panel bucket.

features.name: SM-2 scheduler with monotonic-interval floor
features.detail: Pure function scheduleSm2: grade->q (again=2,hard=3,good=4,easy=5); EF'=EF+(0.1-(5-q)(0.08+(5-q)*0.02)) clamped >=1.3; q<3 lapse resets interval=0/reps=0/due=today/lapses++; success base=firstIntervalDays|6|round(interval*newEase), hard x0.6, easy x1.3, then floor max(newInterval, oldInterval+1) so successful recall never shrinks or plateaus.

jank.symptom: Empty-app problem: 'Nothing due right now' for 144 of the first 200 days; one new concept per week, 98 days to reach the last of 26
jank.root_cause: Unlock bar == mastery bar: a concept unlocks only when EVERY item of EVERY prereq reaches the 7-day interval, and the bundled course is near-linear (2 root nodes). Progression is gated on the calendar, not effort — documented as a pedagogy decision, not a bug (the 'recalled once' alternative opens all 26 on day 0).

Trellis (/mnt/tera/working/programming/OpenHearth/Trellis, Flutter ~2900 lib LOC, v1.0.0+3) is the sole reader of the .ohcourse line (ADR-0008; ohPrimer retired, its reading engine dropped not ported). Loop: import/bundle a .ohcourse -> course map with mastery + prereq locks -> study session (RSVP intake, then recall items) -> self/auto grade -> SM-2 reschedules -> mastery unlocks downstream concepts. Local-first: no network calls at all; storage is entirely SharedPreferences behind CardRepository ('cards:<courseId>' JSON blob of itemId->{ease,intervalDays,dueEpochDay,reps,lapses}) and CourseRepository ('imported_ids' + 'course:<id>' raw JSON; bundled via assets/courses/index.json).

Rebuild-critical semantics: (1) SM-2 in whole UTC epoch days: q(again/hard/good/easy)=2/3/4/5; EF'=EF+(0.1-(5-q)(0.08+(5-q)*0.02)), clamped >=1.3; q<3 = lapse (interval 0, due today, reps 0, lapses++, relearned same session via end-of-queue requeue with cleared inputs); success: base = firstIntervalDays(reps0) | 6(reps1) | round(interval*newEase), hard x0.6 / easy x1.3, then the monotonic floor newInterval=max(that, oldInterval+1) — a successful recall must never shorten OR plateau the interval (repeated Hard once decayed 7,6,5,4,3,2... un-mastering and re-locking nodes; the +1 avoids the plateau). (2) Mastery: item mastered iff interval>=7 days; node mastery = fraction mastered; node unlocked iff every prereq at mastery 1.0 — but the lock applies only to first exposure (a started node never re-locks in the queue). (3) Grading: cloze/discrimination auto (normalized exact match / index); qa/procedure keyword-coverage suggestion (<=0 again, <0.5 hard, <0.85 good, else easy; no-anchor: empty->again else good) with honest self-rating driving the SRS. (4) Parser: schemaVersion '1.0' only; strict on required fields per type, tolerant on optionals; rejects unknown/self/cyclic prereqs with path-qualified errors; never half-imports.

Also shipped: ORP-pivot RSVP reader (dwell-weighted, 150-800 WPM), genanki-faithful native-only .apkg export (subdeck per node, stable sha1 guids), encrypted .ohbk sanctuary backup (bundled-course progress included, content only for imported; destructive index-last restore; startup vault snapshot), no-remote-fetch markdown/LaTeX rendering, bundled 26-concept Kalman course. 132 test cases encode the invariants — the monotonic-interval property and unlocked-never-relocks property tests are the crown jewels to port verbatim.

# Fleet precedent inventory (for reuse by a web-stack app)

## 1. Parlour — single-file PWA + WebView-shell APK — REUSABLE, the fleet's proven web-stack pattern

**PWA** (`/mnt/tera/working/programming/OpenHearth/Parlour/`):
- Pure-logic game modules in `games/*.mjs` (no DOM/network/timers), tested with `node:test` (~276 tests, zero runtime deps). `build.mjs` finds every `export`, strips the keyword, wraps each file in a namespaced IIFE (`const HEXCODLE = (function(){…})();`) and inlines it at the `/*__GAMES__*/` marker in `index.template.html` → generated `index.html` (never hand-edited) (`Parlour/build.mjs`, `Parlour/AGENTS.md`).
- Offline: `sw.js` app-shell cache (`parlour-v1`), stale-while-revalidate over `['./', 'index.html', 'manifest.webmanifest', 'icon.svg']` (`Parlour/sw.js`).
- Deploy: the repo's static files on `master` ARE the site at `levitatingflyfisher.github.io/Parlour/`; workflow is `npm test && npm run build`, commit source + regenerated `index.html` together. No CI deploy automation in-repo, deliberately (`Parlour/docs/how-to/ship-pwa-and-apk.md`).
- Non-negotiables enforced by policy/tests: zero network calls after load, no accounts/ads/tracking, game logic stays pure (`Parlour/AGENTS.md`).

**Shell APK** (`/mnt/tera/working/programming/OpenHearth/ParlourShell/` — a separate, unpublished Flutter repo, forked from the Trellis shell):
- One file, `lib/main.dart`: `webview_flutter` `WebViewController` loading the **live** PWA URL (`https://levitatingflyfisher.github.io/Parlour/`), JS unrestricted, background set to the PWA theme color, `PopScope` walks WebView history before exiting. The PWA's own service worker gives the APK offline play; updates propagate on next shell load with no APK rebuild (`ParlourShell/lib/main.dart`).
- Signing: **debug keystore** in the release build (`signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug")`), `applicationId com.openhearth.parlour` (namespace still `com.openhearth.trellis` from the fork) (`ParlourShell/android/app/build.gradle.kts`). Distributed as a GitHub Release asset `Parlour.apk` via `releases/latest/download/` (`Parlour/docs/how-to/ship-pwa-and-apk.md`).

## 2. DomovoiDiscernment (`OpenHearth/DomovoiDiscernment/`)

**The one resumable-download engine** (`lib/src/transfer/resumable_transfer.dart`) — PATTERN reusable, CODE not (Dart+dio, and the doc comment says "native builds only; web surfaces keep their own inert variants"):
- **Not content-addressed.** Resume = HTTP `Range: bytes=N-` from the `.part` file length; a 416 (partial > resource) deletes and restarts; a 200-instead-of-206 on resume also restarts (appending onto stale bytes would corrupt).
- **Integrity is the caller's `promote` callback**, not the engine's: completion IS the caller's atomic `.part → final` rename (and optional sha check/gunzip) inside `promote` — "never a size judgment". Error anywhere (transfer or promote) is the future's error.
- **Progress contract**: `(receivedBytes, totalBytes?)`, offset by `resumeFrom` so the caller tracks the whole file; `total` null/-1 when the server omits Content-Length. Stream variant is **cold** (nothing hits the wire until subscribed), one listener, `onOutcome` fires exactly once before close with `completed | cancelled` — cancel keeps the partial and `promote` never runs. A JS port is straightforward (fetch + Range + IndexedDB/OPFS), but you rewrite it.

**Brain seam** (`lib/src/brain.dart`) — trivially portable interface: `abstract class Brain { Future<String> complete(String prompt); }` + `AskException(message, {cause})` where message is user-displayable, cause stays in logs. On-device / stove / BYOK-cloud implementations all hide behind it; callers never know which.

**Stove protocol** (`docs/reference/stove-protocol.md`, `lib/src/keys.dart`, `lib/src/stove/`):
- Plain HTTP on LAN, port **4663** ("HOME" on a keypad), server binds `InternetAddress.anyIPv4` (`stove_server.dart:68`).
- Key: BIP39 phrase → standard 512-bit seed (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iters, salt "mnemonic") → HKDF-SHA256, no salt, info `openhearth.domovoi.stove.v1` (FROZEN) → 32-byte frame key. **The secret IS the pairing** — no key crosses the wire (`keys.dart`).
- Exchange: `GET /stove/status` (cleartext probe) → `GET /stove/challenge` (16 random bytes b64, 60s TTL, single-use, 256 max outstanding → 503) → `POST /stove/ask` with cleartext `x-stove-challenge` header + AEAD frame body. Frame = `nonce(12) ‖ ciphertext ‖ mac(16)`, ChaCha20-Poly1305 IETF, AAD = `"domovoi-stove/v1" | endpoint | challenge` (endpoint ∈ {ask, answer}) — no replay across endpoints/versions/asks. Every failure is a constant-shaped `403 refused`; 1 MiB ask cap; 30s body deadline.
- **JS feasibility**: the cipher is the small problem — ChaCha20-Poly1305 is absent from WebCrypto but solved by libsodium.js (`crypto_aead_chacha20poly1305_ietf_*`) or the zero-dep pure-JS `@noble/ciphers`; HKDF-SHA256 and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 are **native WebCrypto** `deriveBits`. A **Node.js** stove client is fully feasible today. A **browser** client is NOT, for two non-crypto reasons: (a) the Dart server emits no `Access-Control-*` headers and the custom `x-stove-challenge` header + octet-stream POST forces a CORS preflight (`OPTIONS`) the server would 404 — grep of `stove_server.dart` finds no CORS handling; (b) an https-served PWA cannot fetch `http://` LAN addresses (mixed content / Private Network Access). A browser client needs server-side CORS + a serving-context answer first.

## 3. sanctuaryAuth — OHBK wire format — FORMAT fully portable to JS; no yellow paper exists

Spec-by-code in `/mnt/tera/working/programming/OpenHearth/packages/sanctuary_auth_core/` (the `OpenHearth/sanctuaryAuth/` dir holds only PRD/spec markdown; `docs/` has no yellow paper — the authoritative wire format is `lib/src/backup/ghost_backup.dart`):
- **OHBK v2**: `[4B magic "OHBK"][1B version 0x02][1B suite 0x01=ChaCha20-Poly1305 IETF][12B nonce][16B Poly1305 MAC][N ciphertext]`. AAD = `header ‖ utf8(context)`; default context `'ghost-backup/v1'`, distinct labels per purpose block cross-context blob substitution. v1 (no AAD) still importable, never emitted. Min blob 34 B, max 10 MB both directions (fail closed at export).
- **Key derivation** (`lib/src/crypto/key_derivation.dart`): 64-byte BIP39 seed → HKDF-SHA256 (no salt, 32-byte out) with frozen info strings; per-app isolation via `appDomain` → `openhearth.<appDomain>.<purpose>.v1` (`^[a-z0-9]+$`, reserved-word guard so `appDomain='sync'` can't collide with the frozen legacy `openhearth.sync.encryption.v1`). Five keys: masterEncryptionKey, syncKey, authKey, recoveryKey, syncChannelId. Plus `deriveKey(secret, domain)` for arbitrary non-BIP39 secrets.
- **JS feasibility: same verdict as the stove** — byte layout is trivial `DataView` work; HKDF/PBKDF2 native in WebCrypto; only ChaCha20-Poly1305 needs libsodium.js or @noble/ciphers. Nothing here needs a network, so no CORS problem — an OHBK reader/writer in the browser is entirely feasible.

## 4. ohStyle — tokens — DIRECTLY web-consumable

`/mnt/tera/working/programming/OpenHearth/ohStyle/openhearth_tokens/tokens.css` (with a `tokens.ts` twin) ships CSS custom properties: Hearth terracotta ramp (primary `--oh-hearth-500: #A85040`), Linen warm neutrals (bg `#FBF8F4`, card `#F5EFE6`, text `#2C1810`), Sage success, Slate info, amber/red accents; hearth-dark + neutral "night" surface palettes; spacing 4/8/16/24/40/64; radii 4–16 + full; type `--oh-font-heading: 'Lora', Georgia, serif` / `--oh-font-ui: 'Nunito', system-ui`; warm linen-tinted elevation shadows; motion durations 80–400 ms; semantic tokens with a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block. Flutter twin is `openhearth_design` (`OhColors`), kept in sync by C1. Known trap: Lora+Nunito lack `≤`/`≥` glyphs (the C7 origin story).

## 5. Landing deploy model — REUSABLE

`/mnt/tera/working/programming/OpenHearth/_ohsite_build/` is a git checkout of **`levitatingflyfisher/levitatingflyfisher.github.io`** (user-pages repo, `master` served from root) — a single 244-line static `index.html`, self-hosted Fraunces+Nunito (`fonts/fonts.css`; explicit "no Google Fonts egress from the front door" comment), inline light/dark palette. Cards render client-side from a JS `APPS` array: each entry = `{name, icon (inline SVG), kind, desc, c1/c2, pwa, apk?, desktopBuilds?, soon?}`. Buttons are platform-typed by color: copper `btn-web` → PWA, pine `btn-apk` → `github.com/<owner>/<Repo>/releases/latest/download/<App>.apk`, slate `btn-desktop` → glean (desktop-only detection via `matchMedia(min-width:900px) and (pointer:fine)` + UA OS sniff), `btn-na` for unavailable. **Trellis card today** (lines 170–175): trellis-lattice SVG in `#C47B6A`/`#A85040`, kind "Spaced repetition", `pwa: …github.io/Trellis/`, `apk: …/Trellis/releases/latest/download/Trellis.apk`. Adding a web app = one `APPS` entry + push to master.

## 6. oh_fleet_conformance C1–C7 — Flutter/Dart-only; VALUES portable, code not

`/mnt/tera/working/programming/OpenHearth/packages/oh_fleet_conformance/` runs inside `flutter_test` via one `runFleetConformance(FleetAppConfig(...))` file (README). Checks: **C1** style single-source (canonical `openhearth_design` by sibling path, no vendored forks/retyped hex); **C2** backup retention (sanctuary_backup_ui ≥0.2.0, shared `BackupEnvelope` serializer); **C3** size budgets (`budgets.json` vs gzipped `main.dart.js` + arm64 APK, measure–budget–ratchet); **C4** exact Android `<uses-permission>` surface both directions **incl. the release merged manifest** — the no-INTERNET / zero-permission claims are tests, not promises; **C5** a11y sweep at 320 dp × 3.0 text scale incl. opened dialogs; **C6** harness canon (flutter_test_config, analysis_options, CI pinning the fleet Flutter version); **C7** fonts (opt-in via `FleetAppConfig.withBundledFonts`, absent from `defaultChecks`) — every printed character must exist in the bundled font cmaps, with emoji + never-drawn parser character-classes exempt, and written to fail-on-nothing-found (`lib/src/checks/fonts.dart`, `lib/src/fleet_conformance.dart:32,94`). A web-stack app can't run any of it directly but should re-pin the same values: token single-source, size budgets, no-network-as-a-test, 320dp/3× a11y, glyph coverage.

# 2026 Browser / On-Device ML Landscape — Research Report

## 1. transformers.js v3.x (and the v4 surprise)

**Version reality check:** v3 (Oct 2024) introduced WebGPU support ("up to 100x faster than WASM"), the full dtype menu (fp32, fp16, q8/int8/uint8, q4, bnb4, q4f16) with per-module dtype for encoder-decoder models, and the move to `@huggingface/transformers` ([v3 blog](https://huggingface.co/blog/transformersjs-v3)). **Transformers.js v4 shipped Feb 9, 2026** with a completely rewritten C++ WebGPU runtime co-developed with the ONNX Runtime team, tested across ~200 architectures, and WebGPU now also works in Node/Bun/Deno ([v4 blog](https://huggingface.co/blog/transformersjs-v4), [releases](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js/releases)). Any new project should target v4, not v3.

**Multilingual Whisper models + quantized sizes** (all on onnx-community, multilingual, encoder + decoder-with-past pairs; sizes from HF file trees):

| Model | Practical quantized total | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| whisper-tiny | **~41 MB** (int8) | enc int8 10.1 MB + dec int8 30.5 MB ([tree](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/whisper-tiny/tree/main/onnx)) |
| whisper-base | **~77 MB** (int8) | enc int8 23.2 MB + merged dec int8 53.7 MB ([tree](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/whisper-base/tree/main/onnx)) |
| whisper-small | **~248 MB** (int8) | enc int8 92.3 MB + dec int8 156 MB ([tree](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/whisper-small/tree/main/onnx)) |
| whisper-large-v3-turbo | **~563 MB** (q4f16) | enc q4f16 370 MB + dec q4f16 193 MB; enc int8 645 MB, fp32 enc 2.55 GB ([tree](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo/tree/main/onnx), [model](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo)) |

Note the q4 decoder anomaly on small models: tiny's q4 decoder (86.6 MB) is *larger* than its int8 (30.5 MB) — int8/q8 is the right pick below small.

**Pipeline options:** the ASR pipeline accepts `language` (ISO hint), `task: 'transcribe' | 'translate'` (translate = X→English only, inherited from Whisper), `return_timestamps: true | 'word'`, and `chunk_length_s` / `stride_length_s` (canonical long-audio recipe: 30 / 5 overlapping windows) ([AssemblyAI walkthrough](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/offline-speech-recognition-whisper-browser-node-js), [pipeline docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers.js/api/pipelines)).

**Word-level timestamps — real but rough:** word-level requires special `_timestamped` ONNX exports that keep cross-attentions (e.g. [whisper-large-v3-turbo_timestamped](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo_timestamped); announced as "Whisper Timestamped: multilingual + word-level" by [Xenova](https://huggingface.co/posts/Xenova/386072637398041)). Open wounds: WebGPU pipeline + word-level was a long-running gap ([#820](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js/issues/820)); turbo_timestamped shipped with broken timestamps (Jul 2025, [#1357](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js/issues/1357)); accuracy complaints ([#805](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js/issues/805)); WebGPU fp16 encoder precision degrades output (Mar 2026, [#1590](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js/issues/1590)) — run the encoder fp32/int8 on WebGPU. **Streaming:** no true streaming word timestamps; chunk callbacks (`on_chunk_start/end`) only fire with `return_timestamps: true`, not `'word'` ([#1198](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js/issues/1198)). Long audio is chunked, not streamed.

## 2. whisper.cpp → WASM

Mature but CPU-bound: the official whisper.wasm example does **~2-3x realtime for tiny/base on a modern CPU**, supports models only up to `small`, caps the demo at 120 s audio, greedy sampling only, and has no GPU path in the browser ([whisper.wasm README](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/blob/master/examples/whisper.wasm/README.md)). transformers.js + WebGPU beats it substantially (a 76 MB model at 5-8x realtime claimed by [whisperstt](https://whisperstt.com/blog/transcribe-audio-in-browser/); comparison overview at [OfflineTTS](https://offlinetts.com/blog/browser-speech-recognition-whisper-comparison/)). whisper.cpp has native token-level timestamps, but in-browser the ecosystem has consolidated on transformers.js (e.g. [browser-whisper](https://github.com/tanpreetjolly/browser-whisper) wraps transformers.js with WASM fallback). Verdict: whisper.cpp WASM is the fallback for non-WebGPU browsers, not the primary path.

## 3. In-browser text LLMs

- **WebLLM** (`@mlc-ai/web-llm`): WebGPU-required, Apache-2.0, 18.5k stars; fastest in-browser inference (Phi-3.5-mini at 71 tok/s per its [paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.15803v2)); prebuilt MLC weights include Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B/4B ([mlc-ai/Qwen3-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/mlc-ai/Qwen3-0.6B-q4f16_1-MLC)); lags newest architectures (Qwen3.5 Gated-DeltaNet unsupported, open request [#778](https://github.com/mlc-ai/web-llm/issues/778)); loads whole model through JS memory ([repo](https://github.com/mlc-ai/web-llm)).
- **wllama**: llama.cpp WASM binding, **V3 added WebGPU + multimodal**; auto single/multi-thread; 2 GB ArrayBuffer limit worked around by `llama-gguf-split` 512 MB chunks; streams model from OPFS into buffers (more memory-efficient than WebLLM); MIT, active ([repo](https://github.com/ngxson/wllama), [comparison](https://localmode.dev/blog/three-llm-providers-one-api)).
- **Smallest useful models:** Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct — **Apache-2.0, ungated**, 0.49B params, 32k context, ~500 MB q8, "runs in 1-2 GB browser memory, handles basic classification" ([HF](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), [maddevs](https://maddevs.io/writeups/running-ai-models-locally-in-the-browser/)). Llama-3.2-1B: gated behind the Llama community license on HF. **Gemma-2-2b-it: gated** — accept-Google's-terms wall, "gemma" license, actually ~3B params ([HF](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-2b-it)). For a FLOSS no-account product, Qwen (2.5/3) is the only friction-free family.

## 4. Translation done small

- **opus-mt per-pair** (Xenova conversions, e.g. [opus-mt-en-es](https://huggingface.co/Xenova/opus-mt-en-es/tree/main/onnx)): en-es quantized runs ~52 MB (int8 encoder) + ~60 MB decoder ≈ **~110 MB per direction per pair**; many pairs are smaller (the folk "40-80 MB" number matches the older v2 `quantized` single-file totals for smaller pairs). Fast, decent for high-resource pairs, but one model per direction.
- **NLLB-200-distilled-600M** ([Xenova conversion](https://huggingface.co/Xenova/nllb-200-distilled-600M)): 200 languages, one model, but **>800 MB download and 2-5 s per complex sentence** at 8-bit in browser ([alexop.dev build report](https://alexop.dev/posts/building-client-side-ai-translator-vue/)); WebGPU use has open issues ([#1286](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js/issues/1286)), plus a pruning bug history ([#843](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js/issues/843)). Coverage vs weight: NLLB wins coverage, opus-mt wins size/speed.
- **Newer + small:** Chrome's built-in **Translator API** — stable since Chrome 138, on-device models downloaded by the browser (not your quota), Edge 148 too, but **desktop-only, not on mobile** and Chromium-only ([Chrome docs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/translator-api)). Good progressive enhancement, not a foundation.

## 5. Browser TTS

- **kokoro-js** (powered by transformers.js): Kokoro-82M v1.0 ONNX — fp32 326 MB / fp16 163 MB / **q8 92.4 MB** / q4f16 154 MB, `dtype` selectable, Apache-2.0; the **ONNX/browser package exposes 28 voices, American + British English only** — the 9-language claim belongs to the Python model with espeak G2P, not the JS path ([Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX), [Xenova announcement](https://huggingface.co/posts/Xenova/503648859052804), [hexgrad/kokoro](https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro)). Quality: best-in-class for the size; near-commercial for short EN clips ([review](https://www.visionstory.ai/open-source/kokoro-tts)).
- **Piper WASM**: whole pipeline (phonemizer + ONNX) compiled to WASM, ~60 MB voices, CPU-only (no WebGPU needed), 3-5x realtime, 22.05 kHz, MIT; multiple maintained forks ([piper-tts-web](https://github.com/Mintplex-Labs/piper-tts-web), [Poket-Jony fork](https://github.com/Poket-Jony/piper-tts-web), [overview](https://offlinetts.com/tts/piper/)). This is the multilingual browser-TTS answer (Piper's voice catalog spans dozens of languages), at lower naturalness than Kokoro.
- **SpeechT5** in transformers.js ([Xenova/speecht5_tts](https://huggingface.co/Xenova/speecht5_tts)) works but is English-only and audibly a generation behind both — legacy option.

## 6. Storage + PWA platform reality (2026)

- **Quotas** ([MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage_API/Storage_quotas_and_eviction_criteria)): Chrome/Edge — up to **60% of disk per origin** (best-effort *and* persistent). Firefox — 10% of disk capped at 10 GiB best-effort; 50% of disk if persistent. Safari — **~60% of disk for Safari and Home-Screen web apps** (~15% inside in-app WebViews). **OPFS counts against the same quota** and follows the same eviction. Eviction is whole-origin, LRU.
- **Safari 7-day eviction**: script-writable storage (IndexedDB, localStorage, SW registrations, Cache) deleted after 7 days of no interaction — **but Home-Screen-installed web apps are exempt in practice: they keep their own usage counter separate from Safari** ([Apple dev forums](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/710157), [MagicBell 2026 guide](https://www.magicbell.com/blog/pwa-ios-limitations-safari-support-complete-guide)). Installing is the mitigation; iOS can still purge a PWA's storage after weeks of disuse.
- **`navigator.storage.persist()`**: Chrome/Safari auto-grant based on engagement heuristics, Firefox prompts; on Chrome it upgrades to only-user-can-clear ([MDN persist()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/StorageManager/persist)). On iOS its protection against the 7-day timer is under-documented; developers report it helps, don't bet on it.
- **iOS install post-DMA**: Apple announced removal of EU Home-Screen web apps in iOS 17.4 beta ([Register](https://www.theregister.com/2024/02/16/apple_web_apps/)), then reversed and kept them, WebKit-based ([Apple DMA support page](https://developer.apple.com/support/dma-and-apps-in-the-eu/)). Third-party engines via BrowserEngineKit exist on paper; **zero browsers have shipped one as of early 2026** ([MobiLoud 2026 guide](https://www.mobiloud.com/blog/progressive-web-apps-ios)).
- **Safari WebGPU: shipped and default-on in Safari 26 / iOS 26** (Sept 2025); all major browsers now ship WebGPU by default ([implementation status](https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/wiki/Implementation-Status), [webgpu.com](https://www.webgpu.com/news/webgpu-hits-critical-mass-all-major-browsers/)). Caveat: only on up-to-date iOS.
- **Long jobs (40-min transcription)**: background-tab *timers* get clamped (500 ms/2 s/5 s tiers), but **Web Worker threads are not throttled in background tabs** — compute continues ([supercharge](https://www.superchargebrowser.com/features/js-throttling/), [getintechs](https://www.getintechs.com/blog/inactive-tab-throttling), [Medium](https://medium.com/@adithyaviswam/overcoming-browser-throttling-of-setinterval-executions-45387853a826)). Android Chrome may still freeze/discard whole tabs under memory pressure; iOS Safari suspends the entire page (workers included) when backgrounded — there is no true background processing on iOS PWAs ([MagicBell](https://www.magicbell.com/blog/pwa-ios-limitations-safari-support-complete-guide)). Practical design: run inference in a worker + hold a **Screen Wake Lock** in the foreground. Wake Lock is now universal (Safari 16.4+, >94% global support; [caniuse](https://caniuse.com/wake-lock), [web.dev](https://web.dev/blog/screen-wake-lock-supported-in-all-browsers)); the installed-iOS-PWA wake-lock bug was fixed in iOS 18.4 ([Progressier](https://progressier.com/pwa-capabilities/screen-wake-lock)).

## 7. FSRS vs SM-2

FSRS-6 with per-user optimization reaches mean log loss 0.344 and **beats SM-2 in 99.6% of benchmark collections**; simulations on 500M+ real Anki reviews show ~20-30% fewer reviews for equal retention ([Neurako digest of srs-benchmark](https://www.neurako.com/blog/fsrs-vs-sm2-spaced-repetition-algorithms-compared), [flica](https://flica.app/article/fsrs-vs-sm2)). Honest caveats from the same sources: the 20-30% figure is simulation, not an RCT, and SM-2 had to be retrofitted with probability formulas to be comparable. **ts-fsrs** ([repo](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/ts-fsrs)): implements FSRS-6, MIT, ~740 stars, Node ≥20, actively released; **scheduling works out of the box with default parameters fit on hundreds of millions of reviews — per-user parameter fitting is a separate package** (`@open-spaced-repetition/binding` optimizer), so a Trellis-style app can ship FSRS with defaults and add fitting later.

## 8. Podcast/RSS from a serverless PWA — the CORS reality

Arbitrary feeds and enclosures mostly don't send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so `fetch()` from a PWA fails; `<audio src>` *can play* cross-origin but the page can't read bytes (no offline caching, no transcription input). What serverless players actually do: require a reverse proxy ([pager](https://github.com/flysteur-dev/pager) — "requires at least a reverse proxy to get around CORS"), pre-fetch via CI ([rssTea](https://github.com/avadhesh18/rssTea) uses GitHub Actions), go P2P/WebTorrent ([HackerNoon single-file app](https://hackernoon.com/how-i-built-a-complete-p2p-rss-podcast-app-in-a-single-html-file-uo1631z1)), or fall back to public CORS proxies ([Wilburn's podcast client](https://thomaswilburn.github.io/wc-book/cs-radio.html)).

**The donor comms layer** (`/mnt/tera/working/programming/OpenHearth/ohPrimer/rebuild/src/scripts/40-comms.js`) is a complete, battle-designed version of that last strategy: SSRF guard (`assertSafeFetchUrl`) before every fetch; direct-first with a short 5 s timeout ("CORS failures are fast, hangs are not"); an explicit, profile-scoped **consent gate before any public proxy is used** (cors.eu.org → allorigins.win → codetabs.com), with the prompt naming exactly which third parties would see the URL; background feed refresh *never* prompts — proxies only if already consented; size caps (25 MB text, 300 MB audio, enforced mid-stream via reader with progress callbacks); conditional GET with ETag/Last-Modified, plus 304/404/410/429+Retry-After handling; and a documented note that media hosts (pdst.fm, megaphone.fm, transistor.fm) don't send CORS headers so `<audio>` plays but `fetch()` needs the proxy. This is the reference design for "no server, still honest about egress."

# Learning-Product Prior Art — Web Research Report

All claims cite URLs. Organized by the six questions, ending with consolidated steal/refuse lists.

## 1. Language-from-content tools (LingQ, Readlang, Language Reactor, Migaku)

**Core shared mechanic — the known-word ledger.** LingQ tags every token in a lesson by familiarity: blue = never seen, yellow = "LingQed" (learning), white = known; a known word can be demoted back to learning with one click (https://www.lingq.com/blog/lingq-review/, https://www.lingq.com/blog/reviewing-vocabulary/). This per-word state, persisted across all content, is what makes "read anything and the app knows what's new *to you*" work. LingQ reviews words via SRS with five activities (flashcards, reverse, cloze, dictation, multiple choice) (https://www.lingq.com/blog/reviewing-vocabulary/). Every lesson pairs text with native-speaker audio — read, listen, or both — which is the closest existing thing to the "stop in one format, resume in another" idea (https://www.lingq.com/blog/lingq-review/).

**Readlang** is the minimal version: an eReader where clicking a word (or click-dragging a phrase) translates it in place, and every translation automatically becomes a flashcard carrying original context, translation, and source; its SRS uniquely uses corpus word-frequency as a scheduling input, so common words surface sooner (https://readlang.com/features, https://www.mezzoguild.com/readlang-review/, https://www.lingualift.com/blog/read-more-languages-with-readlang-review/).

**Language Reactor** overlays Netflix/YouTube with dual subtitles, click-to-define, auto-pause after each subtitle line, and slowdown; export and deeper dictionaries are behind a paid Pro tier (https://www.classcentral.com/report/review-language-reactor/, https://funfluen.com/learn/compare/language-reactor-vs-migaku/). **Migaku**'s one-click card capture is the gold-standard mining UX: one click saves sentence + audio + screenshot + translation into a flashcard deck, exportable to Anki (https://funfluen.com/learn/compare/language-reactor-vs-migaku/).

**What requires a server:** LingQ is server-bound — users report that losing WiFi means no lessons at all, a long-standing complaint (https://forum.lingq.com/t/offline-mode-for-android/27278). Migaku requires an account and subscription; its offline story is partial (flashcards sync media for offline study, but the pipeline is account-gated) (https://www.bestaitools.com/tool/migaku/, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.migaku.android). Nothing in the *mechanics* (per-word state, click-to-define, context capture) inherently needs a server — the server dependence is dictionaries/MT lookups and account sync, both replaceable with on-device dictionaries and local models. Sentence mining itself, as the community defines it, is just "whole sentences from content you consume, kept as flashcards with meaningful context" (https://forum.lingq.com/t/what-is-sentence-mining/35586).

## 2. SuperMemo incremental reading

**Mechanics worth stealing** (from SuperMemo's own docs): (a) read many articles *incrementally* — every article is a queue element, you read a portion and move on (https://help.supermemo.org/wiki/Incremental_reading); (b) **extracts** (Alt+X) split articles into smaller child portions that inherit context and get their own review schedule; **clozes** (Alt+Z) turn a sentence into Q/A via deletion (https://www.super-memory.com/archive/help15/read.htm); (c) a **priority queue** where every element carries a 0–100% priority and review order is priority-sorted with deliberate randomization mixed in (https://help.supermemo.org/wiki/Priority_queue); (d) *incremental* cloze generation — don't make all clozes from an extract at once; make one now, another at next review (https://help.supermemo.org/wiki/Priority_queue).

**Known failure modes, from SuperMemo's own documentation and secondary analysis:** too much randomization unravels prioritization and drops high-priority retention; strict priority sorting lets new material permanently displace old (https://help.supermemo.org/wiki/Priority_queue). The priority scale itself is a usability trap — "nearly everyone asks" why top priority is 0% not 100%, and SuperMemo's docs openly admit the software "makes life of beginners hard because it does not compromise learning efficiency for sleekness" (https://super-memory.com/help/il_full.htm). Independent empirical validation of IR's claimed gains is thin — mostly anecdote and SuperMemo's own user data — and the technique demands heavy up-front processing investment (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incremental_reading, https://grokipedia.com/page/Incremental_reading). Lesson: steal extracts + priorities + interleaving, but hide the machinery behind defaults; never expose a 0-is-highest percent scale.

## 3. Mnemonic medium (Matuschak/Nielsen) + the memory literature

**Quantum Country / Orbit.** The text breaks every few hundred words for embedded review prompts; days later you're re-prompted, on an efficiently expanding schedule (days → weeks → months) (https://notes.andymatuschak.org/Mnemonic_medium, https://quantum.country/). Orbit is the general-purpose platform for writing in this medium (https://notes.andymatuschak.org/z4RTpQqeT7JkxyaV7WwBJ2b). Matuschak's notes stress that the medium "gives structure to normally-atomized prompts" — prompts live inside a narrative, not as orphan cards (https://notes.andymatuschak.org/z8e98xn7t5QNHr5cf8oqjbJ) — and warns explicitly against "orphan prompts" disconnected from context (https://notes.andymatuschak.org/zKPv6qkSErdRGqyryvgS2wS?stackedNotes=z8QtbrR4cxDshTYBq3RCfwUVkXS8mSjRmAnqk).

**Prompt-writing principles** from "How to write good prompts" (https://andymatuschak.org/prompts/): good prompts are **focused** (one detail), **precise** ("vague questions elicit vague answers"), **consistent** (same answer every time, else retrieval-induced forgetting inhibits neighbors), **tractable** (~90% accuracy), and **effortful** (must actually retrieve from memory — recognition isn't retrieval). Anti-patterns named there: long cloze passages that train pattern-matching on the question's *shape*; binary yes/no prompts (minimal effort, shallow); orphan facts with multiple defensible answers. It also invokes the **generation effect** — "you remember information better when you generated it yourself" — recommending prompts that ask the reader to *generate* novel examples, and endorses writing your own prompts to build "understandings of your own" beyond the author's (https://andymatuschak.org/prompts/). This is the direct answer to "highlighted flashcards had no construction behind them": the fix is prompts embedded in the discourse, authored with these properties, plus a generation step for the reader.

**Literature anchor:** Dunlosky et al. 2013 (*Psychological Science in the Public Interest*) rates **practice testing (retrieval) and distributed practice as high-utility**, **elaborative interrogation** (generating "why/how" explanations) and interleaving as moderate-utility/promising, and **highlighting and rereading as low-utility** (https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/1529100612453266, https://www.aft.org/ae/fall2013/dunlosky). Retrieval's long-term-retention benefit is among the best-replicated effects in the field (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0959475217301810). So: a study feature built on highlight-then-flip-cards sits on the two *worst*-rated techniques; one built on retrieval + spacing + "why does this follow?" prompts sits on the best.

## 4. FSRS / Anki ecosystem norms

FSRS is now native in Anki (23.10+), replacing SM-2, achieving equal retention with ~15–20% fewer reviews (https://studycardsai.com/blog/anki-fsrs-algorithm, https://faqs.ankiweb.net/frequently-asked-questions-about-fsrs.html). The single user-facing knob serious users expect is **desired retention** (allowed 0.70–0.99; 0.90 recommended for most) (https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/fsrs4anki/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md, https://faqs.ankiweb.net/frequently-asked-questions-about-fsrs.html). FSRS models each card as (difficulty, stability, retrievability), and parameters are **optimized per-user from their own review log** (https://expertium.github.io/Algorithm.html). Ecosystem norms: `.apkg` deck export/import and `.colpkg` collection export are the lingua franca; review history must survive export because the optimizer feeds on it (https://faqs.ankiweb.net/frequently-asked-questions-about-fsrs.html). Practical implication: ship FSRS (it's MIT-licensed, `open-spaced-repetition`), expose desired-retention as the one setting, keep the full review log locally, and support `.apkg` both ways — serious SRS users treat lock-in of review history as disqualifying.

## 5. Attention sovereignty

**Zvi's "Out to Get You"** (original at https://thezvi.wordpress.com/2017/09/23/out-to-get-you/): a product is Out to Get You when it seeks your resources — time, attention, money — at your expense, and the key variable is whether its demand is **bounded**. Facebook and free-to-play games are the canonical *unbounded* threats ("wants your entire life"; "can charge tens of thousands"). The four responses: **Get Gone**, **Get Got** (accept, *on purpose*, knowing your maximum loss), **Get Compact** (find a bounded rule that caps exposure, then relax), **Get Ready** (permanent battle-mode vigilance — itself costly: "your brain cannot relax"). Design translation: a trustworthy learning app must present a **bounded, legible ask** — a session has a natural end, the app never escalates its demand — so users can Get Compact instead of Get Ready. The companion essay "Slack" makes the complementary point that systems consuming all slack are corrosive (https://thezvi.substack.com/p/slack).

**Cozy web / digital gardens / RSS:** Venkatesh Rao's "cozy web" names the retreat into non-performative, non-algorithmic spaces (https://playeroneuniverse.medium.com/introducing-the-cozy-web-a-sanctuary-amidst-the-dark-forest-9ce08ce0bec2). Digital gardens are non-linear, evolving, tended-not-fed spaces — "an end to the infinite scroll" (https://www.cccb.org/en/w/articles/digitals-gardens-an-end-to-the-infinite-scroll). The RSS framing is exact: the algorithmic timeline is "a slot machine… optimized for compulsion, not comprehension," while an RSS workflow is "a garden where you choose what to plant, tend it on your schedule, and nothing appears that you didn't select" (https://www.nutshellnewsletter.com/blog/what-is-rss-and-why-it-still-matters); Doctorow's "The web is bearable with RSS" argues the same (https://pluralistic.net/2026/03/07/reader-mode/).

**Duolingo-style dark patterns to refuse:** streaks with paid "repair" (loss aversion as the foundational lever of the whole product) (https://medium.com/@productbrief/duolingos-gamified-growth-how-a-green-owl-turned-language-learning-into-a-14-billion-habit-d47d9fa30a77); guilt-tripping push notifications and mascot shaming (https://opinionsandconditions.substack.com/p/duolingo-owl-dark-patterns-digital-guilt); streak anxiety and compulsive checking displacing the actual learning goal, "Duolingo burnout" (https://dev.to/yaptech/duolingos-shallow-learning-trap-gamified-streaks-harmful-habits-4134); "streak creep" — the streak becomes the point, and metric-keeping crowds out the goal (https://thedecisionlab.com/insights/consumer-insights/streak-creep-the-perils-of-too-much-gamification); competitive leaderboards and appointment mechanics resembling addictive social media (https://dev.to/yaptech/duolingos-shallow-learning-trap-gamified-streaks-harmful-habits-4134). **What legitimately helps:** bite-size sessions and immediately visible progress are consistently credited as the *non-manipulative* part of Duolingo's effectiveness (https://medium.com/@navsrujan-mit/duolingo-gamifying-language-learning-eb8e6a55b521); Readlang's fixed-size review sessions (8/15/25 words) are a bounded-session exemplar (https://www.mezzoguild.com/readlang-review/); FSRS's due-count is itself honest visible progress. The mnemonic medium's expanding schedule is an *appointment the memory math sets*, not one engagement metrics set (https://notes.andymatuschak.org/Mnemonic_medium).

## 6. Podcast-first language learning today

What people actually do: run Whisper (or faster-whisper) locally to generate transcripts/SRT from any audio (https://wellstsai.com/en/post/whisper/, https://localaimaster.com/blog/local-ai-subtitles-whisper); use WhisperX's wav2vec2 forced alignment when timing matters — it tightens word boundaries to roughly ±50 ms, "the difference between subtitles glued to the speech and ones that drift" (https://wellstsai.com/en/post/whisper/); or use packaged players — SubX Player already does fully-offline on-device Whisper/Moonshine subtitle generation with dual subtitles, shadowing, auto-repeat, and sentence mining for local files and podcasts (https://www.subx.app/), and Immersive Translate does it server-side in the browser (https://immersivetranslate.com/en/video/podcast-subtitle-generator/).

**Where it breaks:** (1) **hallucination** — ~1% of Whisper transcriptions contain entirely fabricated phrases, 38% of which carry explicit harms, concentrated in silences and disfluent speech ("Careless Whisper," https://arxiv.org/html/2402.08021v2); mitigation is VAD preprocessing (https://github.com/openai/whisper/discussions/679) or hallucination-suppressed variants (Calm-Whisper, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.12969). (2) **Timestamps** — non-English audio yields wrong/short segment timings and repeated hallucinations (https://github.com/openai/whisper/discussions/1862); verbatim-accurate timing needs specialized models (CrisperWhisper, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.16589). (3) **Low-resource languages** need domain fine-tunes (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.15284). (4) The workflow is **fragmented across tools** — transcribe here, align there, mine into Anki elsewhere — which is exactly the seam a unified local-first app closes.

## Consolidated: patterns to steal
1. Per-word known/learning/new state painted over all content (LingQ) — the engine of "study anything."
2. Click/tap-to-define with automatic context-carrying card creation (Readlang, Migaku's one-click sentence+audio+screenshot capture).
3. Paired text+audio per item with resume-in-either-format (LingQ lessons).
4. Extracts + incremental cloze + priority-with-randomization interleaving (SuperMemo) — behind invisible defaults.
5. Prompts embedded in the reading flow on an expanding schedule; authored to be focused/precise/consistent/tractable/effortful; generation-effect prompts (Matuschak, Quantum Country).
6. Retrieval + spacing + elaborative interrogation as the pedagogical spine; treat highlighting as capture, never as study (Dunlosky 2013).
7. FSRS with a single desired-retention knob, per-user optimization from the local review log, `.apkg` in/out.
8. Bounded-session design (fixed-size reviews, natural stopping points) so users can "Get Compact" (Zvi); tend-not-feed garden framing; user-chosen queue à la RSS.
9. Local Whisper + forced alignment + VAD as the on-device transcript pipeline; on-device subtitle generation is proven shippable (SubX).

## Consolidated: patterns to refuse
1. Streaks as hostage + paid streak repair + loss-aversion scaffolding (Duolingo).
2. Guilt notifications, mascot shaming, appointment mechanics set by engagement rather than by memory math.
3. Leaderboards/competitive social pressure in a study tool.
4. Unbounded asks: infinite feeds, "just one more" queues with no natural end (Zvi's unbounded-demand criterion).
5. Server-gated core function: LingQ's no-WiFi-no-lessons failure; account-gated pipelines (Migaku); export behind a paywall (Language Reactor Pro).
6. SuperMemo's exposed machinery: 0%-is-highest priority scales, pro-optimized UI hostile to beginners, mandatory manual prioritization.
7. Highlight-and-flip flashcards as the study model (low-utility per Dunlosky; orphan prompts per Matuschak).
8. Trusting raw Whisper output blind — silence hallucination and timestamp drift require VAD/alignment before showing a learner a transcript as ground truth.

proposals.architecture:
# Espalier — full design

**One modular TypeScript codebase, web-native.** The single-file era was the jank, not the requirement: ohPrimer's own `rebuild/` already proved the porting method (7 modules, 108 node tests, verbatim extraction + issue-ID regression tests). Espalier finishes that thought at full scale, welds in Trellis's study semantics verbatim, and rebuilds the ML layer from first principles on transformers.js v4.

## 0. Thesis

Everything the user takes in — podcast episode, article, EPUB chapter, feed item, pasted text, generated passage — becomes a **Work threaded on one spine**: an ordered list of sentence-grade spans. Text, audio, transcript, and translation are **layers addressed by the same span IDs**. Position is a spine address, not a layer address — so you stop listening in the car and resume reading at the same sentence, possibly in another language. Study items anchor to span ranges, so no card is ever an orphan prompt (Matuschak's law). The LLM is a seam, never a resident: it distills, converses, and grades **only when asked**, and its distillation output must pass the same strict `.ohcourse` parser as any human-authored course — the openDaisugi instinct (verify what the LLM authored) applied to curriculum.

## 1. Stack (with maturity evidence)

- **Language/build:** TypeScript strict, Vite, ES modules, zero runtime CDN — every dependency vendored and bundled (the esm.sh-outage-bricks-ML failure mode dies here).
- **View:** Preact (+ @preact/signals) — ~4KB, a decade stable; the reader surfaces (RSVP, minimap, scroll reconciliation) stay hand-rolled canvas/DOM exactly as the donor proved out.
- **ML:** `@huggingface/transformers` **v4** (Feb 2026, rewritten C++ WebGPU runtime, ~200 architectures — per the research packet, target v4 not v3); `kokoro-js` (Kokoro-82M ONNX); `piper-tts-web` (Mintplex-Labs fork, MIT, CPU WASM); `wllama` V3 (llama.cpp WASM+WebGPU, OPFS streaming, MIT); `@mlc-ai/web-llm` (18.5k stars) as an optional lazy chunk for big-desktop discourse; `@ricky0123/vad-web` (Silero VAD, ~2MB) for hallucination suppression.
- **Study:** own verbatim SM-2 port (default) + `ts-fsrs` (FSRS-6, MIT, ~740 stars, ships default parameters) behind one Scheduler interface.
- **Crypto:** `@noble/ciphers` (zero-dep ChaCha20-Poly1305 IETF) + native WebCrypto HKDF-SHA256/PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 — exactly the gap analysis in the fleet packet (OHBK + stove need only the AEAD filled in).
- **Parsing:** JSZip (EPUB — donor precedent), pdfjs-dist, tesseract.js (lazy, OCR fallback), fflate (zips), `@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm` (~1.2MB lazy) for in-browser genanki-faithful `.apkg`.
- **Tests:** Vitest + fake-indexeddb + Playwright; visual-loop skill for screenshot review.

## 2. Module map

```
espalier/
  src/
    core/        # Result, typed events, epoch-day time, ids
    tokens/      # ohStyle tokens.css + tokens.ts import (C1: single source)
    spine/       # Work, Span, Layer, Alignment, Position — THE model
    store/       # typed IDB wrapper, schema+migrations, OPFS blob store, quota/eviction
    comms/       # fetch policy: SSRF guard, consent gate, proxies, conditional GET, caps
    intake/      # epub, pdf+ocr, text/md heuristics, url-article, gutenberg, reading-list, tokenizer
    feeds/       # subscriptions, discovery, refresh hygiene, auto-download, river, OPML
    reader/      # rsvp, parafoveal, scroll, speak, toc, minimap, page panel, context strip, sentinels
    audio/       # player bar, chapters (JSON+PSC), offline cache, timing sync
    ml/          # model registry, download engine, InferenceHost worker protocol, asr/translate/tts adapters
    jobs/        # checkpointed resumable job engine (transcribe/synthesize/distill/download/ocr)
    study/       # scheduler seam (SM-2 verbatim + ts-fsrs), grading, 4 item types, DAG, session, revlog
    courses/     # .ohcourse 1.0/1.1 strict parser, repository, distillation validator
    brain/       # LLM seam: Null/Byok/OllamaLocal/Wllama/WebLLM/Stove providers + router
    discourse/   # comprehension checks, Socratic follow-ups, explain-back, distillation pipeline
    profiles/    # multi-profile, parent dashboard + PIN, per-profile scoping
    backup/      # OHBK v2 read/write, legacy trellis/ohPrimer import, anki csv+apkg, vault snapshot
    ui/          # screens: Hearth, Shelf, River, Reader, Espalier(course map), Tend(review), Kiln(jobs)
    pwa/         # sw (shell cache + COOP/COEP injection), manifest, install, share-target
  workers/       # inference.worker.ts, jobs.worker.ts (real files, not blob URLs)
  tests/         # vitest unit, behavior (playwright), goldens, budgets
```

Dependency rule (enforced by a lint test): `spine`, `study`, `courses`, `backup`, `intake` parsers, and `comms` policy are **pure** — no DOM, no IDB, no fetch; effects live in `store`, `jobs`, `ui`. This is what made Parlour and the Trellis domain layer testable, kept.

## 3. Content spine data model (requirement 2, the heart)

```ts
Work   { id, kind: 'book'|'article'|'episode'|'note'|'generated', title,
         provenance {url?, feedId?, courseId?, model?}, langGuess,
         ephemeral: boolean, decayAt?, pinned, createdAt }
Span   { seq, blockIdx, kind: 'text'|'heading'|'code'|'table'|'figure', hash }   // sentence-grade
Block  { idx, kind, tocEntry? }                                                  // paragraph-grade, sentinels preserved
TextLayer  { workId, lang, role: 'original'|'transcript'|'translation'|'summary',
             chunks: SpanTextChunk[] }        // ~200 spans/record — bounds rewrite cost
AudioLayer { workId, blobRef(OPFS), duration, provenance: 'enclosure'|'tts:<voice>'|'file',
             timing: chunked span→[t0,t1], wordTiming?: experimental, confidence }
Position   { profileId, workId, spanSeq, tokenOffset, mediaTime?, mode, updatedAt }  // OWN tiny store
CardAnchor { workId, spanRange, focusTokens }  // every card deep-links to context
```

- **Format switch:** mediaTime→span via timing map→reader opens there; span→t0 the other way; translation layers share span IDs so switching language keeps the exact sentence. TTS layers are synthesized per-span, so their timing is intrinsic.
- **Alignment sources:** Whisper segment timestamps give sentence-grade alignment natively (the reliable multilingual path); translation alignment is 1:1 by span (NLLB/opus-mt called per-span, as the donor's translation strip already did per-block); EPUB/article spans come from the ported tokenizer's segment map.
- **Ephemera decay by default:** feed items and cached episodes carry `decayAt` (per-feed keepN/days, donor eviction semantics). Any work that is read-progressed, extracted-from, carded, or pinned is **promoted** (`ephemeral=false`) and persists. Works persist; ephemera compost. This is attention sovereignty in the schema, not in a setting.
- **Positions/translations split out** of the work record — the donor's "position autosave rewrites megabytes" jank is fixed structurally.

## 4. Storage

- **IndexedDB `espalier` v1** stores: works, spanChunks, textLayerChunks, audioLayers(meta), positions, extracts/cards, revlog(append-only), courses, feeds, episodes(meta, **guid+profileIdx stamped on write** — fixes the donor's orphan jank), jobs, profiles, settings, consents.
- **OPFS** for all big bytes: episode audio, TTS caches, figure blobs, **model files**, backup vault snapshots. IDB-blob fallback where OPFS is absent (old WebViews).
- **Multi-profile scoping** on every store; profile delete cascades everything including episodes and TTS caches (donor bug fixed).
- **Quota citizenship:** `navigator.storage.persist()` requested on install; storage panel shows per-bucket usage (models/audio/works/courses) with per-feed purge; 80% quota warnings; auto-download respects metered + quota (donor semantics kept). Quota realities from the packet (Chrome 60%/origin, Firefox 10GiB best-effort, Safari ~60% but 7-day eviction unless installed) are surfaced honestly in the storage panel copy: "install to home screen to protect your library" on iOS.
- **Migrations:** versioned, tested with fake-indexeddb fixtures.

## 5. ML runtime

**Worker architecture:** real module workers (no blob-URL eval). One `inference.worker` owns all model sessions behind a typed request/response protocol (`InferenceHost` interface) with transferables, streamed progress events, and per-task cancellation via AbortSignal (v4 supports it — the donor's "cancel merely abandons the promise" dies). A `MockHost` implements the same interface for tests. Sticky fallback flags are replaced by per-task retry with cooldown + explicit user retry (donor jank fixed). Eviction is **platform-aware**: memory budget probed (deviceMemory, iOS heuristic); desktop keeps 2–3 sessions resident, iOS keeps 1 (donor's evictExcept behavior as the floor, not the ceiling).

**Threading/backends:** WebGPU where present (all major browsers ship it default-on in 2026, incl. Safari 26 per the packet). Where absent, multithreaded WASM — GH Pages sends no COOP/COEP, so our service worker injects `COOP: same-origin` + `COEP: credentialless` (coi-serviceworker technique; all assets same-origin so nothing breaks). Whisper encoder pinned int8/fp32 on WebGPU per issue #1590 (fp16 encoder precision bug).

**Model registry:** a vendored manifest of pinned model files (HF resolve URLs), sizes, sha-256, licenses — all chosen models are **Apache-2.0/MIT and ungated** (no token walls in a no-account product; Qwen not Gemma/Llama, per the packet). Downloads land in OPFS via the download engine (§6) and transformers.js v4 is pointed at that cache — a browser-cache eviction can never silently re-trigger 600MB again.

Per-tier model table → see ml_plan. Long-audio recipe: 30s windows / 5s stride (the canonical chunking), Silero VAD pre-pass to skip silence (kills the ~1% hallucination concentration in silences), language picker + auto-detect stored on the work record, Whisper's built-in `task:'translate'` (X→English) exposed as a one-tap "rough English" layer.

## 6. Reliability engineering

**Download engine — the domovoi laws ported to TS** (pattern, not code, exactly as its doc comment instructs): resume = HTTP `Range` from OPFS `.part` length; 416 or 200-on-resume → discard and restart (never append onto stale bytes); integrity + atomic `.part→final` rename live in the caller's `promote` callback (sha-256 vs registry manifest); progress `(received, total?)` offset by resumeFrom; cancel keeps the partial; cold stream; `onOutcome` fires exactly once. UI: real MB totals, honest ETA, a **persistent resume card** in the Kiln for any partial, metered-connection warning, consent naming exact sizes (donor's consent gate kept verbatim).

**Job engine — every long operation is a checkpointed, persisted Job:**
```ts
Job { id, kind: 'transcribe'|'download'|'synthesize'|'distill'|'ocr'|'feedSweep',
      params, checkpoint, progress {done,total,unit,etaMs}, state, error? }
```
Jobs run in a dedicated worker (worker threads are NOT throttled in background tabs, per the packet; Screen Wake Lock — universal since iOS 18.4 — held while foreground), survive reload/crash via IDB, and resume on boot. **Transcription specifically:** enclosure streams to OPFS (never a 300MB RAM buffer); decode proceeds in chunks (WebCodecs AudioDecoder where present; MP3 frame-boundary slicing + decodeAudioData fallback for Safari; whole-file decode only below a size threshold); each 30s window commits its segments to `checkpoint.segments` with `decodedThroughSec`; the partial transcript is **visible and readable while the job runs**; a killed 40-minute transcript resumes at its last window, never restarts. Completion promotes segments atomically into a TranscriptLayer. TTS synthesis is the same shape: per-span WAV chunks cached in OPFS keyed (work, voice, spanSeq), playback starts when the first sentence is ready (streaming — the donor's 5–15-minute wait dies), partial cache is usable. Kiln screen = all jobs, honest progress, pause/resume/cancel.

## 7. Study engine — Trellis semantics verbatim, then exceeded

**Ported exactly (with its property tests):** SM-2 in whole UTC epoch days; q(again/hard/good/easy)=2/3/4/5; EF′=EF+(0.1−(5−q)(0.08+(5−q)·0.02)) clamped ≥1.3; lapse resets interval/reps, lapses++, same-session relearn requeue with cleared inputs; success base = firstIntervalDays | 6 | round(interval·EF′), hard ×0.6 / easy ×1.3, then the **monotonic floor max(that, oldInterval+1)**; mastery = interval ≥7d; node mastery = fraction; unlock iff every prereq at 1.0; **unlock-is-first-exposure-only** (a started node never re-locks); grading: normalizeAnswer, cloze exact-all-blanks, discrimination index, keywordCoverage with 0.5/0.85 thresholds, suggestion-only-highlights-a-button; clozeKeysInTextOrder; the four item UIs (cloze/qa/discrimination/procedure) with hints/sources/rung chips. The monotonic-growth-under-repeated-Hard and unlocked-never-relocks property tests port **verbatim** as the crown jewels.

**Exceeded:**
1. **Revlog** — append-only review history per card (Trellis's admitted gap). Enables FSRS optimization later and honest Anki interchange (serious SRS users treat review-history lock-in as disqualifying, per the packet).
2. **FSRS-6 opt-in** via ts-fsrs behind the same `Scheduler` interface, default parameters, one knob (desired retention, default 0.90). Mastery maps to stability ≥7d; unlock-first-exposure-only makes re-lock impossible under either scheduler. SM-2 remains the default so `.ohcourse` semantics and the deterministic test suite stay exact.
3. **The empty-app fix** (144-of-200-days jank): review sessions come in bounded servings (8/15/25, Readlang precedent); when the garden is tended, the end screen offers (a) the next locked node's intake **as reading**, and (b) an explicit "sprout ahead" that starts ONE node early, flagged, never counted as mastery, never unlocking downstream. Course authors can set `gate: strict|standard` in 1.1; the default preserves Trellis exactly.
4. **Construction & discourse** (§9) — retrieval + elaboration on top of the typed items, per Dunlosky's high-utility list.
5. Extract-to-card (donor flow: swipe-up, drag-select focus span, V-flag vocab) now creates **typed** items with span anchors — every card can jump back into its source context, and "hear this sentence in the episode" works when the source has an audio layer.

## 8. .ohcourse 1.0 / 1.1

The 1.0 strict/tolerant parser ports with its full rejection matrix (schemaVersion '1.0' only, per-type required fields, unknown/self/cyclic prereqs rejected with path-qualified errors, never half-imports). **1.1 adds only optionals** (1.0 files remain valid): `discourse` per item (followUps[], explainBack{prompt,rubric}, misconceptions[]), `anchors` (span refs into a source work), `gate: strict|standard`, and `diagramMermaid` finally **rendered** (lazy mermaid chunk) instead of parsed-and-ignored. Import via paste, file picker, share-target, and deep link. The bundled Kalman starter course ships as an asset. Courses distilled by the LLM must pass this same parser — repair loop ≤2 attempts, then honest failure.

## 9. LLM seam (requirement 4)

Domovoi's Brain seam, ported: `interface Brain { complete(req): Promise<string>; stream?(req): AsyncIterable<string>; caps: {ctx, local, name} }` + `AskException` (displayable message, cause logged). Providers: **NullBrain** (T0 — every discourse affordance hides, nothing breaks), **ByokBrain** (Anthropic direct-browser or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — donor's callLLM + test-connection kept), **OllamaBrain** (local endpoint, egress-consent-exempt per donor's isLocalEndpoint law), **WllamaBrain** (Qwen2.5-0.5B q8 in-tab for utility tasks), **WebLlmBrain** (Qwen3-1.7B/4B on strong WebGPU desktops), **StoveBrain** (household desktop — honest status in ml_plan/risks). A router assigns task classes: distillation prefers big-context providers (stove/BYOK), cloze-making and keyword-grade assists run on the 0.5B.

**Three discourse moments:**
- **Distill-time (works at T0):** distillation writes followUps/explainBack/misconceptions INTO the course, so a potato-phone student gets construction-and-discourse study with zero runtime inference. This is the single most important design move for the potato floor.
- **Review-time (T2+/BYOK/household):** post-reveal Socratic follow-up ("why does this hold?"), explain-back grading annotated PASS/REVIEW — **never overrides self-rating** (Trellis law preserved).
- **Reading-time:** donor's comprehension check upgraded with generation-effect prompts ("give your own example").

**Distillation pipeline** (a Job): source Work → chunked map (concept candidates + span anchors) → reduce (DAG + typed items + discourse) → strict-parser validation → editable review screen (per-node accept) → import. Anki-grade provenance: every node keeps its span anchors.

## 10. Feeds & comms

The rebuild's `40-comms.js` is already the reference design and ports near-verbatim to TS: SSRF guard before every fetch (schemes, loopback/link-local/private/metadata hosts), direct-first with 5s timeout, **consent-gated public proxies naming exactly which third parties see the URL**, background refresh never prompts, 25MB text / 300MB audio / 8MB XML caps enforced mid-stream, conditional GET (ETag/Last-Modified), 304/404/410/429+Retry-After, 5-failure breaker. Feed discovery, iTunes directory, OPML both ways, auto-download queue (metered + quota aware), river view (reverse-chron only, unread/audio/text filters, capped read-tracking) — all donor semantics kept. `<audio src>` streams cross-origin without a proxy (playback never needs consent; only byte-reads do). Optional self-hosted proxy URL setting for households that run one. Desktop Tauri phase removes the proxy need entirely.

## 11. Attention sovereignty by structure

No analytics module exists; there is nothing to toggle. Reverse-chron only; the sole badge is the due count (memory math, not engagement math). Bounded sessions with a natural end ("The garden is tended."). No streaks, no repair purchases, no mascot guilt, no leaderboards — a calendar of days-tended is shown plainly, loses nothing when broken. Ephemera decay is default-on. An **egress ledger** screen (WeatherGlass precedent) enumerates every possible network egress and its consent state; a Playwright test asserts **zero requests post-load without consent** — the C4 spirit, re-pinned as a web test.

## 12. Backup & migration

**OHBK v2 in TS** against the wire format in `ghost_backup.dart`: `OHBK|0x02|0x01|nonce12|mac16|ct`, AAD = header‖utf8(context), ChaCha20-Poly1305 IETF via @noble/ciphers, BIP39→PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512(2048,"mnemonic")→HKDF-SHA256 with `openhearth.espalier.<purpose>.v1`. **Cross-implementation golden fixtures generated by the Dart core prove byte compatibility both ways.** Study data (courses, cards, revlog, profiles, settings, feeds-as-OPML) fits the 10MB envelope; the full library exports as `.ohbka` — a zip of ≤10MB OHBK envelopes + manifest (honest about the format cap). Weekly silent vault snapshot to OPFS when a key exists (Trellis law). **Legacy import:** Trellis-domain `.ohbk` (appDomain 'trellis', aadContext 'trellis-backup/v1' — courses+cards map 1:1) and ohPrimer plaintext JSON backups (books/extracts/feeds, with the donor's prototype-pollution sanitizer). The standard data hop is `.ohbk` (fleet law: no backwards-compat theater); a ~40-line optional shell bridge that one-shot-reads the surviving `shared_prefs` XML from the same package dir is a Phase-F nicety, not a dependency. Anki: CSV (donor format) + genanki-faithful `.apkg` **on all surfaces** via sqlite-wasm — exceeding Trellis, which hid it on web.

## 13. Surfaces

1. **PWA** — repo `Espalier`, deployed Parlour-style (static files on master ARE the site) at `levitatingflyfisher.github.io/Espalier/`; landing APPS entry swaps the Trellis card. SW: app-shell cache + COOP/COEP injection + offline toasts; share-target for .ohcourse/.ohbk/audio files; `?url=` deep link kept.
2. **Android** — `EspalierShell` forked from ParlourShell: one main.dart, webview_flutter at the live PWA URL, PopScope back-nav, applicationId **com.openhearth.trellis, versionCode 4** (> Trellis's +3) — sideload upgrades the existing install base in place; released as `Espalier.apk` via releases/latest/download. First-run offers "Restore from a Trellis backup".
3. **Desktop (post-1.0)** — Tauri wrapping the same dist; sidecars: whisper.cpp + llama.cpp native binaries for T3-class local inference without browser limits; native StoveBrain (no CORS problem outside the browser); real filesystem import/export.

## 14. Signature UI

ohStyle tokens as the single source (tokens.css/tokens.ts imported, C1 spirit; Lora/Nunito self-hosted; the ≤/≥ glyph trap gets a cmap test — C7 ported). Print-like heritage: linen ground, Lora serif measure, drop caps on works, terracotta accents, warm shadows, dark "night-linen" scheme. **The signature:** a thin copper **reading thread** — the same spine-position element rendered in the reader margin, the audio bar, and the translation strip, visibly the *same thread* as you switch formats; and the **espalier course map** — nodes as grafts trained along horizontal wires (tiers of the DAG), bare wood = locked, swelling bud = due, blossom = started, fruit = mastered. Screens: Hearth (home/profiles), Shelf (library), River (feeds), Reader, Espalier (course), Tend (review), Kiln (jobs). Full donor a11y parity: focus-trapped modals, OpenDyslexic + high contrast, reduced-motion, 320dp × 3× text-scale sweep as a test.

## 15. Test strategy

- **Unit (Vitest):** the rebuild's 108 tests port first (same modules, TS); Trellis's invariant matrix ports verbatim (exact SM-2 values, ease floor, monotonic-Hard property, unlocked-never-relocks 30-Hard property, lapse-only-shrink, purity, grading boundaries 0.5/0.85, cloze ordering, parser rejection matrix incl. cycle paths, corrupt-store tolerance). Target ≥450 unit tests by v0.1.
- **Cross-implementation goldens:** OHBK fixtures emitted by the Dart sanctuary core, decrypted by TS and vice versa; `.apkg` structure fixtures vs Trellis's exporter; `.ohcourse` acceptance corpus shared with Trellis.
- **Store:** fake-indexeddb + OPFS mock; migration fixtures.
- **ML seam:** InferenceHost protocol tested against MockHost (checkpoint commits, cancellation, progress) — the donor's lesson that the riskiest layer had zero tests, answered structurally; one tagged-slow CI lane runs real whisper-tiny WASM on a 30s fixture.
- **Behavior (Playwright):** port the donor's 11, add: resume-across-format, reload-mid-transcription-resumes-from-checkpoint, zero-egress-without-consent (request interception), review serving flow, offline install.
- **Budgets & conformance ports:** gzipped shell JS ≤300KB pre-ML (ML lazily chunked), measured in CI (C3); token single-source lint (C1); glyph cmap coverage (C7); 320dp/3× a11y sweep (C5); visual-loop screenshots at 360/768/1280.

## 16. Build phases

- **P0 (wk 1–2) Bench:** repo, Vite/TS/Vitest/Playwright, tokens, store+migrations, spine model, port rebuild's 7 modules + 108 tests.
- **P1 (wk 3–4) Reader:** RSVP/parafoveal/scroll, TOC/minimap/page panel/context strip/sentinels, positions store, Shelf, EPUB/PDF+OCR/TXT/URL/Gutenberg intake, share/deep-link. Installable PWA.
- **P2 (wk 5–6) Garden:** study engine verbatim + property tests, .ohcourse parser, espalier map, 4 item UIs, revlog, FSRS opt-in, Anki CSV+apkg, OHBK + legacy imports, profiles + parent PIN.
- **P3 (wk 7–9) Kiln:** download engine, model registry, InferenceHost, **multilingual checkpointed transcription** + VAD + timing sync, audio bar + episode caching, feeds/river/auto-download. **← v0.1, first delicious release: the friend-studies-their-podcast-in-its-language story works end to end.**
- **P4 (wk 10–11) Voices:** translation strip (opus-mt default, NLLB opt-in, next-N prefetch), streaming TTS (Kokoro/Piper/Web Speech), synthesis cache.
- **P5 (wk 12–13) Discourse:** Brain providers, distillation pipeline + review screen, discourse moments, .ohcourse 1.1.
- **P6 (wk 14) Ship:** budgets, a11y sweep, storage panel, shell APK versionCode 4, landing card, doc spine (VISION/AGENTS/Diátaxis/ADRs/yellow-paper for the spine+checkpoint invariants), optional prefs bridge.
- **Post-1.0:** Tauri + sidecars, stove v1.1 (server CORS/PNA), FSRS per-user optimizer.
